about: proseweave's inventory of English connectives, grouped by the relation each one signals. Independently compiled for proseweave from English grammar and from the category definitions in the published literature: Halliday & Hasan (1976) Cohesion in English, ch. 5 (additive, adversative, causal, temporal conjunction); Quirk, Greenbaum, Leech & Svartvik (1985) A Comprehensive Grammar of the English Language, 8.134-8.144 (conjunct classes: listing, summative, appositive, resultive, inferential, contrastive, transitional) and 14.12 (subordinators); Sanders, Spooren & Noordman (1992) 'Toward a taxonomy of coherence relations', Discourse Processes 15 (basic operation causal/additive, polarity positive/negative, order); Louwerse (2001) 'An analytic and cognitive parametrization of coherence relations', Cognitive Linguistics 12 (additive/temporal/causal x positive/negative); and the intentional/causal cohesion constructs of Graesser, McNamara, Louwerse & Cai (2004). The papers supply the category definitions; the members were chosen by proseweave's authors from general knowledge of English. No word list, data or code from any other tool was consulted or copied. Released under the same licence as proseweave.
format: Each group lists items as space-separated lowercase tokens, matched against a sentence's words longest-first, each word used at most once per index. An item written 'word|a,b' counts only when that occurrence of the word has sense a or b (see 'senses'). An item written 'word#sub' counts only when the word introduces a subordinate clause. Without Jev, a sense falls back to 'by_class' (the word's class from tagging) and then to 'default'. An index may carry 'senses': {word: 'all' | 'none'} to count a sense-dependent word in every sense or in none.

additive.source: Halliday & Hasan 1976, additive conjunction; Quirk et al. 1985, additive (reinforcing) conjuncts; Louwerse 2001, positive additive

and.source: Halliday & Hasan 1976, simple additive 'and'; Quirk et al. 1985, coordinator

similarity.source: Halliday & Hasan 1976, additive: comparison (similar); Quirk et al. 1985, additive conjuncts of equation

alternative.source: Halliday & Hasan 1976, additive: alternative; Quirk et al. 1985, coordinator 'or' and conjunct 'alternatively'

apposition.source: Halliday & Hasan 1976, additive: apposition (expository, exemplificatory); Quirk et al. 1985, appositive conjuncts

emphasis.source: Halliday & Hasan 1976, adversative: avowal (in fact, actually) and additive emphasis; Louwerse 2001, positive additive of assertion

contrast.source: Halliday & Hasan 1976, adversative (proper, contrastive, correction); Quirk et al. 1985, antithetic conjuncts; Louwerse 2001 and Sanders et al. 1992, negative additive

concession.source: Quirk et al. 1985, concessive conjuncts and subordinators; Sanders et al. 1992 and Louwerse 2001, negative causal (denial of expectation)

exception.source: Quirk et al. 1985, subordinators of exception and negative condition; Louwerse 2001, negative causal/conditional

cause.source: Halliday & Hasan 1976, causal: reason; Quirk et al. 1985, subordinators of reason; Sanders et al. 1992, causal (non-basic order)

result.source: Halliday & Hasan 1976, causal: result and inference; Quirk et al. 1985, resultive and inferential conjuncts; Sanders et al. 1992, causal (basic order)

condition.source: Halliday & Hasan 1976, causal: conditional; Quirk et al. 1985, conditional subordinators; Louwerse 2001, causal (conditional)

causal_lexis.source: Graesser et al. 2004 and Sanders et al. 1992: causal relations expressed by verbs and nouns of causation (cause, effect, enabling); base forms

preventive_lexis.source: Sanders et al. 1992 and Louwerse 2001: negative causal relations expressed lexically (prevention, hindrance)

purpose.source: Halliday & Hasan 1976, causal: purpose; Quirk et al. 1985, subordinators of purpose

intention_lexis.source: Graesser et al. 2004: intentional cohesion (goals, plans and actions of agents) expressed by nouns and verbs of intention; base forms

temporal.source: Halliday & Hasan 1976, temporal conjunction (sequential, simultaneous, conclusive, immediate, interrupted, repetitive, specific); Quirk et al. 1985, temporal subordinators and time adjuncts used conjunctively; Louwerse 2001, positive temporal

sequence.source: Quirk et al. 1985, listing (enumerative) conjuncts; Halliday & Hasan 1976, temporal: internal sequence

summary.source: Quirk et al. 1985, summative conjuncts; Halliday & Hasan 1976, temporal: conclusive

transition.source: Quirk et al. 1985, transitional conjuncts (discoursal and temporal)

subordinator.source: Quirk et al. 1985, 14.12: simple subordinators of time, reason, concession and condition; counted only when introducing a clause

causal_lexis_forms.source: Graesser et al. 2004 and Sanders et al. 1992: causal relations expressed by verbs and nouns of causation (cause, effect, enabling); inflected forms of the base group

causal_lexis_wide.source: Wider causative lexis (Quirk et al. 1985 on causative verbs): verbs and nouns naming causation or its outcome

intention_lexis_forms.source: Graesser et al. 2004: intentional cohesion (goals, plans and actions of agents) expressed by nouns and verbs of intention; inflected forms of the base group

intention_lexis_wide.source: Wider intentional lexis (Graesser et al. 2004, intentional actions): verbs of deciding, hoping and choosing

causative_verbs.source: Quirk et al. 1985, 16.52: causative verbs taking a clause of effect; only 'make' and 'let' are listed, since 'have' and 'get' are mostly not causative

addition.definition: Additive conjuncts that add a further point (Quirk et al. 1985, additive; Halliday & Hasan 1976, additive proper and comparison)
addition.selection: groups and sense handling chosen on the even-numbered half of proseweave's validation corpus; scored on the odd half

sentence_linking.definition: Single-word conjuncts that link a sentence or clause to the preceding discourse (Quirk et al. 1985, conjuncts), plus subordinators introducing a clause
sentence_linking.selection: groups and sense handling chosen on the even-numbered half of proseweave's validation corpus; scored on the odd half

order.definition: Listing and summative conjuncts that order the discourse (Quirk et al. 1985)
order.selection: groups and sense handling chosen on the even-numbered half of proseweave's validation corpus; scored on the odd half

reason_and_purpose.definition: Connectives of reason, result and purpose (Halliday & Hasan 1976, causal: reason, result, purpose)
reason_and_purpose.selection: groups and sense handling chosen on the even-numbered half of proseweave's validation corpus; scored on the odd half

all_causal.definition: Causal relations of either polarity, lexical and conjunctive (Sanders et al. 1992; Louwerse 2001)
all_causal.selection: groups and sense handling chosen on the even-numbered half of proseweave's validation corpus; scored on the odd half

positive_causal.definition: Positive causal relations: cause, result, enabling (Sanders et al. 1992; Louwerse 2001)
positive_causal.selection: groups and sense handling chosen on the even-numbered half of proseweave's validation corpus; scored on the odd half

all_additive.definition: Additive relations: addition, similarity, alternative, apposition, emphasis (Halliday & Hasan 1976; Louwerse 2001)
all_additive.selection: groups and sense handling chosen on the even-numbered half of proseweave's validation corpus; scored on the odd half

all_logical.definition: Logical (non-temporal) connectives of every polarity: additive, adversative, causal, conditional (Halliday & Hasan 1976; Louwerse 2001)
all_logical.selection: groups and sense handling chosen on the even-numbered half of proseweave's validation corpus; scored on the odd half

positive_logical.definition: Logical connectives of positive polarity (Sanders et al. 1992; Louwerse 2001)
positive_logical.selection: groups and sense handling chosen on the even-numbered half of proseweave's validation corpus; scored on the odd half

all_temporal.definition: Temporal connectives: sequence, simultaneity, conclusion (Halliday & Hasan 1976, temporal)
all_temporal.selection: groups and sense handling chosen on the even-numbered half of proseweave's validation corpus; scored on the odd half

positive_intentional.definition: Intentional relations: purpose connectives and words of goal and intention (Graesser et al. 2004)
positive_intentional.selection: groups and sense handling chosen on the even-numbered half of proseweave's validation corpus; scored on the odd half

all_positive.definition: Connectives of positive polarity: additive, causal, temporal (Louwerse 2001)
all_positive.selection: groups and sense handling chosen on the even-numbered half of proseweave's validation corpus; scored on the odd half

all_negative.definition: Connectives of negative polarity: contrast, concession, exception (Louwerse 2001; Sanders et al. 1992)
all_negative.selection: groups and sense handling chosen on the even-numbered half of proseweave's validation corpus; scored on the odd half

all_connective.definition: Connectives of every kind (Halliday & Hasan 1976, all four conjunction types plus continuatives)
all_connective.selection: groups and sense handling chosen on the even-numbered half of proseweave's validation corpus; scored on the odd half

opposition.definition: Contrast and concession (Halliday & Hasan 1976, adversative; Quirk et al. 1985, contrastive and concessive conjuncts)

negative_logical.definition: Logical connectives of negative polarity: contrast, concession, exception (Sanders et al. 1992; Louwerse 2001)

options.result: links a result or conclusion: 'and therefore', 'and so' ('It rained, so we stayed in')
options.purpose: introduces a purpose: 'so that', 'in order that' ('Speak up so everyone hears')
options.discourse: opens or resumes talk ('So, where were we?')
options.degree: means 'very' or 'to such a degree' ('so tired', 'so much')
options.proform: stands in for something already said ('I think so', 'and so did she', 'or so')

options.result: introduces a result: 'with the result that'
options.other: any other use ('so that was it', 'so that he...' meaning 'so, that...')

options.time: means 'from a time in the past until now'

options.cause: means 'because' ('As it was late, we left')
options.time: means 'while' or 'at the moment when' ('As she spoke, the door opened')
options.compare: compares or gives a role or manner ('as tall as', 'as a teacher', 'as I said', 'such as')

options.noun: a noun, a period of time ('a while', 'for a while')

options.time: next or afterwards, in a sequence of events
options.infer: means 'in that case' or 'therefore' ('If so, then we win')
options.list: adds the next item in a list or argument ('And then there is cost')
options.point: means 'at that time' ('I was young then', 'by then', 'back then')

options.cause: a conjunction meaning 'because' ('She wept, for he was gone')
options.prep: a preposition ('for you', 'for a year', 'waited for')

options.time: means 'even now' or 'continuing' ('she still lives there')
means 'up to now' or 'so far' ('not yet')

options.contrast: joins or opens with a contrast ('small but strong')
options.other: means 'except' or 'only' ('all but one', 'but a child')

options.time: means 'as soon as' or 'after' ('Once he left, we ate')
options.other: means 'one time' or 'formerly' ('once a week', 'once upon a time')

options.time: introduces a time clause ('when she arrived')
options.other: asks a question or starts a relative clause ('When did...?', 'the day when')

options.transition: opens or turns the discourse ('Now, the second point')

options.concede: concedes or limits a claim ('At least he tried')
options.amount: means 'no fewer or less than' ('at least ten')

options.other: an adjective or adverb of extent ('the overall cost')
means 'think' or 'expect' ('I suppose so', 'be supposed to')

options.transition: a discourse marker opening a reply or turn ('Well, I don't know')
options.other: an adverb, adjective or noun ('did well', 'feel well', 'a well')

options.list: orders a point or event in a sequence ('First, we ...', 'I went there first')
options.other: an ordinal describing a noun ('the first time', 'his first book')

options.list: orders a point in a sequence ('Second, ...')
options.other: an ordinal or a unit of time ('the second day', 'a second')

options.list: orders a point in a sequence
options.other: an ordinal or fraction ('the third man')

options.list: orders a point in a sequence
orders the next point or event ('Next, add salt', 'what happened next')
options.other: describes a noun or means 'beside' ('next week', 'next to')

options.list: orders the last point or event in a sequence ('Finally, ...')
options.other: means 'at long last' after waiting ('she finally agreed')
means 'final', 'previous' or 'endure' ('last week', 'the last one', 'it will last')
